name: Hanan
overview: Hanan was a male leader identified as a non-Levite, mentioned specifically in Nehemiah 10:26. His role is noted among those who sealed a significant covenant document in the book of Nehemiah. While his tribal affiliation is not recorded, his leadership position highlights his importance in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanan means 'gracious' in Hebrew, reflecting a common biblical proper name without an explicit divine bestowal. This name is recorded in Nehemiah 10:26, emphasizing his identity within the covenant community.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hanan was a descendant of Jacob, affirming his Israelite heritage. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented for him.
scriptureSignificance: Hanan's significance lies in his role as a non-Levite leader who participated in the sealing of the covenant detailed in Nehemiah 10. This act symbolizes a collective commitment to God's law during the restoration period after the exile. His inclusion among the leaders underscores the unity and dedication of the Israelite community in renewing their covenantal promises.
